All four creatures share the same basic mechanic. When killed outside their home plane, they instantly gain a new body and revive with all their Hit Points on that plane. The differences are in what happens to the old body and where they return.

| Creature | Trait | Trigger | What happens to the body | Where it revives |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Pit Fiend** | Diabolical Restoration | Dies outside the Nine Hells | Disappears in sulfurous smoke | Somewhere in the Nine Hells |
| **Rakshasa** | Fiendish Restoration | Dies outside the Nine Hells | Turns to ichor | Somewhere in the Nine Hells |
| **Planetar** | Exalted Restoration | Dies outside Mount Celestia | Simply disappears | Somewhere in Mount Celestia |
| **Solar** | Exalted Restoration | Dies outside Mount Celestia | Simply disappears | Somewhere in Mount Celestia |

Sources: Pit Fiend, Planetar, Rakshasa and Solar entries [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

**Key differences:**

- **Fiends vs. angels:** The Pit Fiend and Rakshasa return to the Nine Hells. The Planetar and Solar return to Mount Celestia [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Body reaction among the fiends:** Both fiends return to the same plane, but their bodies leave different remains. The Pit Fiend's vanishes in sulfurous smoke, while the Rakshasa's turns to ichor [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **The angels are identical:** The Planetar and Solar have the same trait, Exalted Restoration, and their bodies just disappear with no smoke or residue described [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Timing:** All four revive instantly, with no delay period [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

None of these entries say what happens if the creature dies on its own home plane. The traits only cover death outside it.

All three monsters use Swallow as a Bonus Action. In each case it targets one Large or smaller creature the monster is grappling, which makes a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target is swallowed and the Grappled condition ends [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

**Number of creatures swallowed and save DC**
- **Purple Worm:** up to three creatures at a time; Strength save DC 19 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Remorhaz:** up to two creatures at a time; Strength save DC 19 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Tarrasque:** up to six creatures at a time; Strength save DC 27 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

**Conditions and damage while swallowed**
- **Purple Worm:** the creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions and Total Cover against attacks and effects from outside. It takes 17 (5d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the worm's turns [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Remorhaz:** the creature is Blinded and Restrained and has Total Cover. It takes 10 (3d6) Acid damage plus 10 (3d6) Fire damage at the start of each of the remorhaz's turns [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Tarrasque:** the creature is Blinded and Restrained, has Total Cover, and also can't teleport. It takes 56 (16d6) Acid damage at the start of each of the tarrasque's turns [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

**Regurgitation**
In each case the trigger is damage dealt on a single turn by a creature inside the monster. The monster must then succeed on a Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn. If it fails, it regurgitates all swallowed creatures, and each lands with the Prone condition [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Purple Worm:** triggered by 30 or more damage; DC 21 Constitution save; creatures fall within 5 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Remorhaz:** triggered by 30 or more damage; DC 15 Constitution save; creatures fall within 5 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- **Tarrasque:** triggered by 60 or more damage; DC 20 Constitution save; creatures fall within 10 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

**If the monster dies**
Swallowed creatures are no longer Restrained and can escape the corpse, exiting Prone. The movement cost differs:
- Purple Worm: 20 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- Remorhaz: 15 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].
- Tarrasque: 20 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md].

Being Blinded gives your attack rolls Disadvantage [DND5eSRD_176-191.md]. The passages show four ways to avoid or offset that.

**1. See without eyes: Blindsight**
Blindsight lets you see within its range even while Blinded, including Invisible creatures, unless the target is behind Total Cover [DND5eSRD_176-191.md]. Sources:
- The Ranger's level 18 Feral Senses gives Blindsight 30 ft. [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
- Animated objects and some summoned forms have Blindsight, but those are creature traits, not player options [DND5eSRD_104-120.md].

**2. Remove the Blinded condition**
- *Lesser Restoration* ends Blinded (Bonus Action) [DND5eSRD_138-154.md].
- *Heal* and *Mass Heal* end Blinded [DND5eSRD_138-154.md].
- Paladin's Restoring Touch can remove Blinded when using Lay On Hands [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
- *Elixir of Health* ends Blinded [DND5eSRD_204-229.md].

**3. Get Advantage to cancel the Disadvantage**
Advantage and Disadvantage on the same roll cancel out. You then roll one d20, no matter how many sources of each you have [DND5eSRD_001-018.md]. Sources of Advantage:
- **The target can't see you.** You have Advantage when a creature can't see you, for example if it is also Blinded [DND5eSRD_001-018.md].
- **You're Invisible.** Your attack rolls have Advantage [DND5eSRD_176-191.md], e.g. via the Hide action [DND5eSRD_176-191.md] or *Invisibility*/*Greater Invisibility* [DND5eSRD_121-137.md].
- **Barbarian Reckless Attack:** Advantage on Strength attacks [DND5eSRD_019-035.md].
- **An ally's Help action** grants Advantage on the next attack against a nearby enemy [DND5eSRD_176-191.md].
- **Effects on the target:**
  - *Guiding Bolt*: the next attack against the target has Advantage [DND5eSRD_138-154.md].
  - *Shining Smite*: attacks against the target have Advantage [DND5eSRD_155-175.md].
  - Stunning Strike, even on a successful save, gives the next attack Advantage [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
  - Paralyzed, Stunned, Restrained, or Unconscious targets are attacked with Advantage [DND5eSRD_176-191.md].
- **Your own features or gear:**
  - Fighter's Studied Attacks [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
  - The Vex mastery property [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].
  - *Foresight* (Advantage on all D20 Tests) [DND5eSRD_121-137.md].

**4. Avoid becoming Blinded by darkness**
Heavily Obscured areas make you Blinded when trying to see into them [DND5eSRD_001-018.md]. These let you see there:
- Darkvision, which treats Darkness as Dim Light [DND5eSRD_176-191.md].
- The Warlock invocation Devil's Sight [DND5eSRD_064-076.md].

**A partial workaround:** Boon of Combat Prowess's Peerless Aim turns a miss into a hit once per turn. It doesn't remove the Disadvantage [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].

**Highest AC without external help: 23**, or **21** if you don't count your own spells.

**Base equipment and features: AC 21**
- Paladins have training with Light, Medium, and Heavy armor and Shields [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
- Plate Armor gives AC 18 [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].
- A Shield adds +2 [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].
- At level 2, a Paladin gains a Fighting Style feat [DND5eSRD_047-063.md]. The Defense feat gives +1 AC while you wear armor [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].
- 18 + 2 + 1 = **21**. Dexterity doesn't matter, because Plate Armor's AC has no Dex modifier [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].

**Adding your own spell: AC 23**
- *Shield of Faith* is on the Paladin spell list [DND5eSRD_047-063.md]. It gives a creature of your choice, which can be you, +2 AC for up to 10 minutes. It requires Concentration [DND5eSRD_155-175.md], [DND5eSRD_104-120.md].
- 21 + 2 = **23**.

**What doesn't raise it further**
- Effects from the same spell cast more than once don't combine [DND5eSRD_104-120.md].
- *Shield* and *Haste* aren't on the Paladin spell list [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
- None of the Paladin's level 20 features add AC: Aura of Protection boosts saving throws, and the Oath of Devotion's Holy Nimbus grants a ward, damage, and sunlight [DND5eSRD_047-063.md].
- The Epic Boon feats in the document don't add AC [DND5eSRD_087-103.md].

**If magic items count as "your own"**
A Rare-or-better item like *+3 Armor* (Legendary) or *+3 Shield* (Very Rare) would add more [DND5eSRD_204-229.md], [DND5eSRD_230-252.md]. I treated those as outside help, since the rulebook leaves starting magic items to the GM [DND5eSRD_019-035.md].

I don't find this in the rulebook. The passages are the System Reference Document 5.2.1, and they never mention the Player's Handbook or what it costs in real life. They only say the SRD itself is provided free of charge under the CC-BY-4.0 license [DND5eSRD_001-018.md].

Where I looked:
- **Legal Information and Contents** [DND5eSRD_001-018.md]: no other products or prices are listed.
- **Equipment, Adventuring Gear** [DND5eSRD_087-103.md]: the closest match is the in-game **Book** item, which costs **25 GP** and weighs 5 lb. It holds fiction or nonfiction, and consulting an accurate nonfiction Book about its topic gives a +5 bonus to related Intelligence (Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion) checks. That price is for a book your character buys in the game world, not the real-world Player's Handbook.

For the real-world price, check a retailer or the publisher, Wizards of the Coast.

# Restoration Abilities Compared

All four creatures have a restoration trait with the same basic mechanism. If one dies away from its home plane, it instantly gains a new body and revives with all its Hit Points somewhere on that home plane. They differ in what happens to the old body and which plane they return to.

## Celestials: Planetar and Solar
- **Trait name:** Both have **Exalted Restoration** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].
- **Trigger:** Dying outside Mount Celestia [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].
- **Body on death:** It simply **disappears** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].
- **Revival location:** Somewhere in **Mount Celestia** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].

The two traits are worded identically.

## Fiends: Pit Fiend and Rakshasa
- **Pit Fiend:** Its trait is **Diabolical Restoration**. If it dies outside the Nine Hells, its body **disappears in sulfurous smoke**, and it revives somewhere in the **Nine Hells** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].
- **Rakshasa:** Its trait is **Fiendish Restoration**. If it dies outside the Nine Hells, its body **turns to ichor**, and it revives somewhere in the **Nine Hells** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].

## Key Differences

| Creature | Trait | Body on Death | Revival Plane |
|---|---|---|---|
| Planetar | Exalted Restoration | Disappears | Mount Celestia |
| Solar | Exalted Restoration | Disappears | Mount Celestia |
| Pit Fiend | Diabolical Restoration | Disappears in sulfurous smoke | Nine Hells |
| Rakshasa | Fiendish Restoration | Turns to ichor | Nine Hells |

1. **Revival plane:** The celestials return to Mount Celestia, and the fiends return to the Nine Hells.
2. **Fate of the body:** The celestials' bodies vanish cleanly. The pit fiend's vanishes in sulfurous smoke. The rakshasa's is the only one that leaves something behind, since it turns to ichor.

Note: every passage shares the same source heading, so each citation above refers to the Traits block of the creature named.

# Swallow: Purple Worm vs. Remorhaz vs. Tarrasque

The passage for the third creature calls it only "the worm" and never names the Purple Worm. I'm assuming that's the stat block you mean.

## Who can be swallowed and how many

All three use a Strength saving throw against a Large or smaller creature they have Grappled. On a failure, the target is swallowed and the Grappled condition ends.

| | Save DC | Max swallowed at once |
|---|---|---|
| Worm | DC 19 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] | 3 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] |
| Remorhaz | DC 19 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] | 2 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] |
| Tarrasque | DC 27 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] | 6 [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions] |

## Conditions and damage while swallowed

All three give a swallowed creature the Blinded and Restrained conditions and Total Cover against attacks and effects from outside the creature [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions][DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Page 8 / 320].

Only the Tarrasque adds that a swallowed creature **can't teleport** [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions].

Damage is taken at the start of each of the swallower's turns:
- **Worm:** 17 (5d6) Acid [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions]
- **Remorhaz:** 10 (3d6) Acid plus 10 (3d6) Fire [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Page 8 / 320]
- **Tarrasque:** 56 (16d6) Acid [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions]

## Regurgitation

Each creature must make a Constitution save at the end of a turn in which it takes enough damage from a creature inside it. On a failure, it regurgitates all swallowed creatures, who land Prone within a set distance.

| | Damage trigger | Con save DC | Landing distance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Worm | 30+ | DC 21 | within 5 ft |
| Remorhaz | 30+ | DC 15 | within 5 ft |
| Tarrasque | 60+ | DC 20 | within 10 ft |

Sources: Worm and Tarrasque [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions]; Remorhaz [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Page 8 / 320].

The Tarrasque also has Legendary Resistance (6/Day). If it fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead, which could let it avoid regurgitating [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Traits].

## If the creature dies

Swallowed creatures lose the Restrained condition and can escape the corpse, exiting Prone, by spending movement:
- **Worm:** 20 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions]
- **Remorhaz:** 15 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Page 8 / 320]
- **Tarrasque:** 20 feet [DND5eSRD_313-332.md §Bonus Actions]

**I don't find this in the rulebook.** None of the passages give a way to remove or avoid Disadvantage on your attacks while Blinded.

**What the passages do say:**
- While Blinded, your attack rolls have Disadvantage [DND5eSRD_176-191.md §Blinded [Condition]].
- Attacking a target you can't see gives Disadvantage, whether you're guessing its location or can hear it but not see it [DND5eSRD_001-018.md §Making an Attack].

**Possibly relevant, but incomplete:**
- When a creature can't see you, you have Advantage on attack rolls against it [DND5eSRD_001-018.md §Making an Attack]. So if your target also can't see you (for example, it's Blinded too), you'd have both Advantage and Disadvantage. These passages don't say how the two interact.
- Spells, special abilities, and other effects can modify your attack roll, and the GM decides whether you have Advantage or Disadvantage [DND5eSRD_001-018.md §Making an Attack]. No specific effect that removes Blinded's Disadvantage is listed.

**What I searched:** the Blinded condition, Unseen Attackers and Targets, the attack procedure, Opportunity Attacks, Defensive Tactics, and Lightly Obscured. The Defensive Tactics options only impose Disadvantage on attacks *against* you [DND5eSRD_047-063.md §Level 7: Defensive Tactics], so they don't apply. To answer this fully, you'd want the rules on combining Advantage and Disadvantage and on senses like Blindsight, which aren't in these passages.

I don't find this in the rulebook. The provided passages don't cover Armor Class.

**What I searched:**

- **Other level 15 and 20 features:** Superior Critical [DND5eSRD_047-063.md §Level 15: Superior Critical], Arcane Apotheosis [DND5eSRD_064-076.md §Level 20: Arcane Apotheosis], and Primal Champion [DND5eSRD_019-035.md §Level 20: Primal Champion] deal with critical hits, Metamagic, and ability scores. None of them affects AC.
- **Armor:** The only mention is that Medium or Heavy armor gives Disadvantage on saves against extreme heat. Armor AC values aren't given [DND5eSRD_192-203.md §Extreme Heat].

To answer this, I would need passages on armor and shield AC values, the Paladin's fighting styles (such as Defense), spells like *Shield of Faith*, and any magic item rules.
